theory.intro: **End behaviour** describes what happens to $y$ as $x\to\infty$ and as $x\to-\infty$. For the general exponential rules $y=k(a^x)+c$ and $y=k(a^{-x})+c$, assume $a>0$, $a\ne1$ and $k\ne0$. One end of the curve approaches its horizontal asymptote; the other end tends to either positive or negative infinity.

steps: Identify whether the base and exponent represent growth or decay as $x$ increases: for $a>1$, $a^x$ grows and $a^{-x}$ decays; for $0<a<1$, these behaviours reverse.
Identify any vertical reflection ($k<0$) and vertical shift ($c$).
State the horizontal asymptote $y=c$ as the limit for the decaying end.
State the behaviour for the growing end ($y\to\infty$ or $y\to-\infty$).

workedExamples.question_text: For $y=4^x$, describe the behaviour as $x\to\infty$ and as $x\to-\infty$, and state the horizontal asymptote.
For $y=5^{-x}$, describe the behaviour at both ends and state the horizontal asymptote. Explain why $y=\left(\frac15\right)^x$ has the same behaviour.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Using the negative-index law:

$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\left(\frac15\right)^x\\&=(5^{-1})^x\\&=5^{-x}\end{aligned}$

Both rules describe the same decreasing curve.

As $x\to\infty$, $5^{-x}\to0$ from above, so $y\to0$.

As $x\to-\infty$, $-x\to\infty$, so $5^{-x}\to\infty$ and $y\to\infty$.

Horizontal asymptote: $y=0$.

workedExamples.question_text:
Describe the behaviour as $x\to\infty$ and as $x\to-\infty$ for each curve.

(a) $y=-5^x$

(b) $y=-2(4^{-x})$
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) The negative coefficient reflects $y=5^x$ in the $x$-axis.

As $x\to\infty$, $5^x\to\infty$, so $y\to-\infty$.

As $x\to-\infty$, $5^x\to0$, so $y\to0$ from below.

(b) The negative coefficient reflects the decreasing curve $y=4^{-x}$ in the $x$-axis; the factor $2$ changes its scale.

As $x\to\infty$, $4^{-x}\to0$, so $y\to0$ from below.

As $x\to-\infty$, $4^{-x}\to\infty$, so $y\to-\infty$.

Both curves have horizontal asymptote $y=0$.

workedExamples.question_text:
For each function, describe the behaviour at both ends and state the horizontal asymptote.

(a) $y=2(4^x)-3$

(b) $y=-2(5^x)+6$

(c) $y=3(4^{-x})-2$

(d) $y=4-2(5^{-x})$
Explain why $y=3(4^x)+2$ approaches $y=2$ but never reaches it or takes a value below it.
workedExamples.solution_text:
For every real $x$, $4^x>0$.

$\begin{aligned}3(4^x)&>0\\3(4^x)+2&>2\end{aligned}$

Thus $y>2$ for every finite $x$.

As $x\to-\infty$, $4^x\to0$, so $y\to2$ from above. The curve approaches the asymptote $y=2$ without reaching it.

workedExamples.question_text:
Describe the long-term behaviour of each model.

(a) A bacterial population is modelled by $N=700(3^t)$, where $t\ge0$ is time in hours.

(b) A radioactive sample has mass $M=90(4^{-t/6})$ grams, where $t\ge0$ is time in years.

(c) An object's speed is modelled by $v=48(1-3^{-t})$ metres per second, where $t\ge0$ is time in seconds. State the limiting speed and explain whether it can be reached or exceeded at a finite time.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) As $t\to\infty$, $3^t\to\infty$, so $N\to\infty$. The model predicts population growth without bound.

(b) As $t\to\infty$, $-t/6\to-\infty$, so $4^{-t/6}\to0$. Therefore $M\to0\text{ g}$.

(c) As $t\to\infty$, $3^{-t}\to0$, so $v\to48\text{ m/s}$.

For every finite $t$, $3^{-t}>0$, so $1-3^{-t}<1$ and $v<48\text{ m/s}$. The limiting speed is approached from below and is never reached or exceeded.

foundation.question_text: For $y=2^x$, describe the behaviour as $x\to\infty$ and as $x\to-\infty$, and state the horizontal asymptote.
For $y=3^{-x}$, describe the behaviour as $x\to\infty$ and as $x\to-\infty$, and state the horizontal asymptote.
For the curve $y=5^x$, state what happens to $y$ when $x$ becomes very large and positive ($x\to\infty$), and when $x$ becomes very large and negative ($x\to-\infty$).
For $y=\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^x$, describe the behaviour as $x\to\infty$ and as $x\to-\infty$.
For $y=-2^x$, describe the behaviour as $x\to\infty$ and as $x\to-\infty$.
foundation.solution_text:
The curve is reflected in the $x$-axis.
As $x\to\infty$, $y\to-\infty$.
As $x\to-\infty$, $y\to0$.

foundation.question_text: For $y=2^x+3$, describe the behaviour as $x\to\infty$ and as $x\to-\infty$, and state the horizontal asymptote.
foundation.solution_text:
The curve is translated up $3$ units.
As $x\to\infty$, $y\to\infty$.
As $x\to-\infty$, $y\to3$.
Horizontal asymptote: $y=3$.

foundation.question_text: Explain why the graph of $y=3^x$ never touches the line $y=0$.
foundation.solution_text:
For any real number $x$, $3^x > 0$.
Since $3^x$ is strictly positive for all $x$, $y$ can never equal $0$.
The curve approaches $y=0$ as $x\to-\infty$ without ever reaching it.

foundation.question_text:
A population of bacteria grows according to $N=500(2^t)$, where $t$ is time in hours.
Describe the long-term behaviour of $N$ as $t\to\infty$.
foundation.solution_text:
As $t\to\infty$, $2^t\to\infty$.
As $t\to\infty$, $N\to\infty$ (the population grows without bound).

development.question_text: For $y=4-3^x$, describe the behaviour as $x\to\infty$ and as $x\to-\infty$, and state the horizontal asymptote.
development.solution_text:
$y=-3^x+4$
As $x\to\infty$, $3^x\to\infty$, so $y\to-\infty$.
As $x\to-\infty$, $3^x\to0$, so $y\to4$.
Horizontal asymptote: $y=4$.

development.question_text: For $y=5(2^{-x})-1$, describe the behaviour as $x\to\infty$ and as $x\to-\infty$, and state the horizontal asymptote.
development.solution_text:
As $x\to\infty$, $2^{-x}\to0$, so $y\to-1$.
As $x\to-\infty$, $2^{-x}\to\infty$, so $y\to\infty$.
Horizontal asymptote: $y=-1$.

development.question_text: For $y=-4(3^{-x})$, describe the behaviour as $x\to\infty$ and as $x\to-\infty$.
For the curve $y=2-3(2^{-x})$, describe the behaviour as $x\to\infty$ and as $x\to-\infty$, and state the horizontal asymptote.
development.solution_text:
As $x\to\infty$, $2^{-x}\to0$, so $y\to2$.
As $x\to-\infty$, $2^{-x}\to\infty$, so $y\to-\infty$.
Horizontal asymptote: $y=2$.

development.question_text: For $y=6(3^x)-5$, describe the behaviour as $x\to\infty$ and as $x\to-\infty$, and state the horizontal asymptote.
development.solution_text:
As $x\to\infty$, $3^x\to\infty$, so $y\to\infty$.
As $x\to-\infty$, $3^x\to0$, so $y\to-5$.
Horizontal asymptote: $y=-5$.

development.question_text:
The temperature $T$ (in $^{\circ}\text{C}$) of a cup of coffee cooling in a room is modelled by $T=22+68(2^{-0.1t})$, where $t$ is time in minutes.
What temperature does the coffee approach as $t\to\infty$, and why?

The mass $M$ (in grams) of a radioactive isotope decays according to $M=80(3^{-t/5})$, where $t$ is measured in years.
State the limiting mass as $t\to\infty$.

mastery.question_text:
A function is given by $f(x) = -3(4^{-x}) - 5$.
Determine the end behaviour of $f(x)$ as $x\to\infty$ and as $x\to-\infty$, and state the horizontal asymptote.
mastery.solution_text:
As $x\to\infty$, $4^{-x}\to0$, so $f(x)\to-3(0)-5 = -5$.
As $x\to-\infty$, $4^{-x}\to\infty$, so $-3(4^{-x})\to-\infty$ and $f(x)\to-\infty$.
Horizontal asymptote: $y=-5$.

mastery.question_text:
The velocity $v$ (in $\text{m/s}$) of a skydiver with air resistance is modelled by $v(t) = 54(1-2^{-0.2t})$ for $t\ge0$.
State the terminal velocity as $t\to\infty$, and explain why the skydiver never strictly exceeds or reaches it.
mastery.solution_text:
As $t\to\infty$, $2^{-0.2t}\to0$, so $v(t)\to54(1-0) = 54\text{ m/s}$.
Terminal velocity: $54\text{ m/s}$.
Because $2^{-0.2t} > 0$ for all finite $t$, $1-2^{-0.2t} < 1$, so $v(t) < 54\text{ m/s}$ for all finite $t$.

mastery.question_text: For $y=7-5(6^{-x})$, describe the behaviour as $x\to\infty$ and as $x\to-\infty$, and state the horizontal asymptote.
mastery.solution_text:
As $x\to\infty$, $6^{-x}\to0$, so $y\to7$.
As $x\to-\infty$, $6^{-x}\to\infty$, so $y\to-\infty$.
Horizontal asymptote: $y=7$.
